newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell says Nigerian oil stations reopen except one.
newsitem.headline: Shell says Nigerian oil stations reopen except one.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Monday that four of its five flow stations shut last week because of communal clashes in the midwestern Delta state had now been reopened.
"They are all flowing except Warri River flow station," a Shell spokesman in Lagos told Reuters.
"Warri River is still closed in and we won't reopen it without the approval of the local community," he added.
The closure of Warri River has reduced Shell's oil production in the area by 2,000 barrels per day.
"Our output in both the east and western sectors are back to normal except for the 2,000 (bpd) shut in by Warri River," the company spokesman said.

Shell declared force majeure on some cargos of Forcados blend due for lifting from April 29th because of the closure of the flow stations during fighting by militant youths over the relocation of a local council headquarters.
Some 20 percent of its Forcados blend of crude oil, roughly 90,000 bpd, was shut in by the closures of the five flow stations at the time.
The Shell spokesman said no cargo had been cancelled as a result of the force majeure, which he said would remain in force until May 28th.
"No cargo is cancelled. There are delays of between one and half to three days on outstanding shippings," he said.
Scores of lives were lost in the conflict in Warri while Shell, the biggest oil operator in Nigeria was forced to close several oil flow stations and to evacuate staff.
The navy and troops have since been deployed in the troubled region to ensure the flow of crude oil, which accounts for more than 90 percent of Nigeria's foreign exchange income.
